faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Things you need to know about KAI Flow

items.question: What is KAI Flow?
items.answer: KAI Flow is an open-source, enterprise-grade AI agent orchestration platform built on the LangChain and LangGraph ecosystems. By combining LLM nodes, memory components, and advanced triggers (Kafka, Webhook, etc.) on a visual canvas, it allows you to bring autonomous assistants with complex logical flows to production without writing code (or by adding custom code).

items.question: Which LLM providers does KAI Flow support?
items.answer: KAI Flow supports all leading LLM providers in the industry including OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, Mistral, HuggingFace, and local models. Models can be configured directly from the visual interface; you can create hybrid flows by orchestrating different models at each step.

items.question: Do I need coding knowledge to use KAI Flow?
items.answer: No. Thanks to the platform's 'low-code' philosophy, you can design complex workflows in seconds using drag-and-drop. However, the ability to add special Python logic (Custom Nodes) is also provided for advanced users, ensuring full flexibility and scalability.

items.question: How does RAG work in KAI Flow?
items.answer: KAI Flow offers built-in vector database support using PostgreSQL and the pgvector extension. You can configure the complete RAG pipeline, which uploads and splits PDF, Web, and text documents and then allows the agent to query this data, via the visual canvas without needing any additional infrastructure setup.

items.question: How do I access the agents I deployed?
items.answer: Every agent workflow is accessible as a REST endpoint through the FastAPI backend. You can also publish it as an embeddable chat widget on your website using the @kaiFlow/widget npm package.

items.question: How can I contribute to KAI Flow?
items.answer: KAI Flow is open source. You can visit the GitHub repository to open issues, send pull requests, or develop new node types. You can review the CONTRIBUTING.md file for the contribution guide.
